title: 1970 AHSME Problem 35
statement: A retiring employee receives an annual pension proportional to the square root of the number of years of his service. Had he served \(a\) years more, his pension would have been \(p\) dollars greater, whereas, had he served \(b\) years more (\(b\ne a\)), his pension would have been \(q\) dollars greater than the original annual pension. Find his annual pension in terms of \(a,\) \(b,\) \(p,\) and \(q.\)

solutions.text:
Let the current pension be \(X=k\sqrt n.\) Since \(X+p=k\sqrt{n+a}\) and \(X+q=k\sqrt{n+b},\) squaring and using \(X^2=k^2n\) gives the first line below. Multiplying its equations by \(b\) and \(a,\) respectively, and subtracting gives the second: \[ \begin{gathered} 2pX+p^2=k^2a,\\ 2qX+q^2=k^2b,\\ 2X(bp-aq)=aq^2-bp^2. \end{gathered} \] Hence \(X=\dfrac{aq^2-bp^2}{2(bp-aq)}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
